purpose: Define when SongChart must re-resolve repository, generated, external-integration and verification state so stale assumptions do not survive across AI sessions, provider changes or stage transitions.
principles: Recheck reuses existing authorities and verification surfaces; it must not create a parallel verifier hierarchy.

Repository/GitHub facts are resolved live, generated projections are regenerated from authored authorities, and provider facts are rechecked only within their declared external-system authority scope.
A successful earlier verification is historical evidence, not permission to skip verification after the verified tree or relevant external capability changes.
New MCP tools, scopes or mutations are denied by default until the owning registry/governance contract explicitly admits them.

session_resume_or_new_ai: read ./songchart ai status --json or equivalent generated project context before substantial writes
authored_authority_change: review generated diff instead of hand-editing generated authority
before_tranche_advance: working tree must be intentional and synchronized
run repository-contracts verification and stage verification on the current tree
do not mark the tranche accepted from an older SHA
before_candidate_or_canonical_closure: regenerate required authority from the exact target tree
rerun canonical governed verification on the exact head
do not mutate the target SHA while closure is running
external_integration_change: recheck official provider documentation or release notes
compare tool/resource/auth/permission/capability surface with the last accepted registry assumptions
review overlap with already connected native tools, CLI, SDK or API
record adoption, compatibility, deferral or retirement before expanding agent permissions

local_or_package_managed.versioning: pin when the distribution supports deterministic version pinning
local_or_package_managed.upgrade_path: reviewed dependency change -> capability/auth diff -> development smoke -> existing impacted verification -> explicit adoption

remote_managed.versioning: do not invent a local version pin when the provider owns deployment
remote_managed.upgrade_path: detect behavior/toolset/auth drift -> compare with official documentation -> update registry/permissions if accepted -> rerun impacted verification

mcp_upgrade_policy.permission_rule: A provider update must never automatically expand development or production mutation authority.
mcp_upgrade_policy.new_capability_rule: Discovery of a new tool/resource does not imply SongChart adoption or permission.
mcp_upgrade_policy.retirement_rule: Remove obsolete MCP/client configuration after active consumers migrate; do not keep duplicate old/new integrations for convenience.
